newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says manufacturing growth slowed in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says manufacturing growth slowed in 1996.

text.p: Malaysia's manufacturing growth slowed to 12.8 percent last year against 14.5 percent in 1995 due to weaker demand for electronics exports, International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz said on Thursday.

The sector still led economic growth, however, contributing 34.5 percent of the country's gross domestic product in 1996 against 33.1 percent in the previous year, the minister said at an annual briefing for industrialists and diplomats.

The economy expanded by 8.2 percent last year for its ninth straight year of growth in excess of eight percent. Gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 9.5 percent in 1995 and the government has forecast GDP growing by 8.0 percent this year.
Manufacturing was the lead growth sector followed by the construction and services industries, Rafidah said.
"The moderation in manufacturing output in 1996 was due to deceleration in the growth of some export-oriented industries, particularly electronics, due to a softening of external demand," she said.
Rafidah expected the electronics sector to rebound this year, saying the investment outlook remains "promising", though she did not give any projections.
She said investment in the manufacturing sector last year leapt to 41.7 billion ringgit ($16.8 billion) against 26.9 billion ringgit in 1995.
But Malaysia's manufactured exports grew by a mere 5.8 percent against 22.9 percent in 1995, she said.

The manufacturing sector is expected to remain the economy's backbone. But the government, concerned over labour shortages, has been promoting high value-added industries and discouraging labour-intensive ones.
She said the Malaysian ringgit's strengthening against the dollar in recent weeks would not affect foreign investment flows into the country.
"We don't see that happening," she said. "People have come in for a whole range of reasons. The ringgit has not really been a factor for them."
The ringgit has risen by nearly two percent against the U.S. dollar since the start of 1997. ($1 = 2.48 ringgit)
